title: Sanofi Eyes Insmed in Potential $43B Deal as Dupixent Patent Clock Ticks
content: Advertisement News|Articles|November 20, 2026 Sanofi Eyes Insmed in Potential $43B Deal as Dupixent Patent Clock Ticks Listen0:00 / 0:00 Key Takeaways A potential $35–$43 billion Insmed purchase would represent one of the largest biopharma transactions since Pfizer–Seagen, and would be challenging to execute as an all-cash deal. Dupixent generated €5.7 billion in Q3 revenue (~40% of group sales), making the early-2030s patent cliff the central strategic driver for external growth. Insmed’s commercial base includes Brinsupri ($400 million Q3 sales) and Arikayce ($124 million Q3; $460–$470 million FY guidance), with 2026 portfolio revenue projected at $1.8–$1.9 billion. TPIP is in Phase 3 across four pulmonary indications, with projected peak annual sales above $6 billion, complemented by earlier programs in RA, IBD, and DMD. Recent moves—Blueprint Medicines acquisition and explicit pipeline triage amid acknowledged decision-making weaknesses—frame the deal thesis, while Insmed’s CFO departure adds execution uncertainty.SHOW MORE Sanofi is exploring a $35B–$43B takeover of Insmed and its blockbuster lung drug Brinsupri as the French pharma giant braces for Dupixent’s looming patent expiration. Advertisement Sanofi is evaluating a potential acquisition of U.S. drugmaker Insmed, according to a Bloomberg report published November 19, with the French pharma giant working with advisers to assess a deal that could be valued between $35 billion and $43 billion. If completed at the high end of that range, it would rank as the largest biopharma buyout since Pfizer’s $43 billion acquisition of Seagen in 2023.Neither company has commented on the report, which cited anonymous sources. Insmed shares surged roughly 18% to $141.87 on the news, while Sanofi shares slipped about 2% to $46.15.The strategic logic centers on Dupixent, Sanofi’s blockbuster biologic for inflammatory conditions including eczema and asthma, which generated €5.7 billion in third-quarter revenue — nearly 40% of Sanofi’s total group sales. The drug is on track toward patent expiration in the early 2030s, leaving a significant revenue hole that CEO Belén Garijo has repeatedly flagged as the company’s defining challenge. Garijo has told investors the organization is squarely focused on managing the post-Dupixent transition over the next decade, with M&A and licensing alongside improved R&D productivity as the primary levers. Its lead product, Brinsupri (brensocatib), a DPP1 inhibitor approved for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, generated $400 million in third-quarter sales alone. The company projects full-year 2026 revenue of $1.8 billion to $1.9 billion across its portfolio, which also includes Arikayce — a treatment for refractory Mycobacterium avium complex lung disease that posted $124 million in Q3 sales with full-year guidance of $460 million to $470 million.The broader pipelineBeyond its marketed products, Insmed carries a pipeline with significant upside. Its lead investigational asset, treprostinil palmitil inhalation powder (TPIP), is in the Phase 3 PALM program across four indications: pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease, pulmonary arterial hypertension, progressive pulmonary fibrosis, and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Insmed projects peak annual sales above $6 billion for TPIP. The pipeline also includes early-stage candidates targeting rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, and Duchenne muscular dystrophy.The price tag, however, is a formidable obstacle. At $35 billion to $43 billion, Sanofi could not fund an all-cash transaction without taking on substantial debt, and analysts have pointed to Insmed’s elevated valuation as the chief barrier to a deal getting done. Bloomberg Intelligence analysts John Murphy and Aude Gerspacher noted that Garijo faces a core challenge familiar to Sanofi: improving a historically underperforming R&D organization while securing new growth sources to fill the Dupixent void.The report adds to a string of strategic moves by Sanofi in recent months. The company completed a $9.5 billion acquisition of Blueprint Medicines in 2025 to build out its rare disease portfolio, and has been vocal about reviewing its pipeline for underperforming assets. On its second-quarter earnings call this year, Sanofi attributed recent pipeline setbacks to weak decision-making rather than weak science — a candid admission that underscored the urgency of its strategic reset under Garijo.Insmed’s CFO Sara Bonstein departed the company on October 30 after nearly seven years in the role, an executive transition that adds a layer of uncertainty ahead of any potential transaction.In September 2025, Pharmaceutica Executive spoke with Sanofi’s then-CEO Paul Hudson on the company’s decision-making process. He explained, “We chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives. People are looking for miracles. I get letters every day saying, ‘tell me you’re working on this disease because the doctors say there is nothing for me.’ That’s why it has to be miracles.”SourceSanofi Weighs Takeover of US Drugmaker Insmed Bloomberg November 19, 2026 https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-19/sanofi-weighs-takeover-of-us-drugmaker-insmed Newsletter Lead with insight with the Pharmaceutical Executive newsletter, featuring strategic analysis, leadership trends, and market intelligence for biopharma decision-makers. content: EX-99.1 2 ef20084500_ex99-1.htm EXHIBIT 99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Insmed Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Update —Total Company Revenues of $524.4 Million for the Third Quarter of 2026— —BRINSUPRI® (brensocatib) Revenues of $400.1 Million for the Third Quarter of 2026, Reflecting 29% Growth Over the Second Quarter of 2026— —ARIKAYCE® (amikacin liposome inhalation suspension) Revenues of $124.4 Million for the Third Quarter of 2026, Reflecting 9% Growth Over the Third Quarter of 2025— —Company Raises 2026 BRINSUPRI Revenue Guidance to $1.35 Billion to $1.4 Billion— —Company Raises 2026 ARIKAYCE Revenue Guidance to $460 Million to $470 Million— — Insmed Launches BRINSUPRI Tablets 25 mg (brensocatib hydrate) for the Treatment of Non-Cystic Fibrosis Bronchiectasis in Japan— BRIDGEWATER, N.J., October 29, 2026 — Insmed Incorporated (Nasdaq: INSM), a people-first global biopharmaceutical company striving to deliver first- and best-in-class therapies to transform the lives of patients facing serious diseases, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided a business update. “The third quarter marked another period of meaningful progress, defined by commercial momentum, regulatory achievements, and advancement across our diversified pipeline,” said Will Lewis, Chair and Chief Executive Officer of Insmed. “BRINSUPRI’s U.S. launch continues to exceed expectations and ARIKAYCE continues to grow while in its ninth year on the market. This performance supports our decision to raise the low end of our full-year 2026 revenue guidance for both products. We were also pleased to receive regulatory approval and launch BRINSUPRI in Japan, a profound milestone for patients living with bronchiectasis. In addition, the FDA’s acceptance of the sNDA for ARIKAYCE in MAC lung disease represents an important step toward expanding access to this therapy for eligible patients, including those that are newly diagnosed or facing recurrent infections. As we advance our Phase 3 TPIP programs across four large indications and progress our early-stage pipeline, we remain focused on delivering meaningful innovation and improving the lives of patients with serious diseases.” Progress and Anticipated Milestones by Therapeutic Area: Respiratory BRINSUPRI • BRINSUPRI global revenue grew 29% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the second quarter of 2026, driven by strong growth in the U.S. market. • In August 2026, Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) approved BRINSUPRI Tablets 25 mg (brensocatib hydrate) for the treatment of non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis (NCFB) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older. • In October 2026, Insmed launched BRINSUPRI Tablets 25 mg, the first and only MHLW-approved treatment for NCFB, in Japan. 1 ARIKAYCE • ARIKAYCE global revenue grew 9% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by strong growth in international markets. • In September 2026, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) accepted Insmed’s Supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) for review of ARIKAYCE for the treatment of Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) lung disease as part of a combination antibacterial drug regimen. The FDA granted Priority Review to the sNDA and set a target action date of January 28, 2027, under the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA). • Insmed plans to submit data from the Phase 3 ENCORE study to Japan’s Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA) in the fourth quarter of 2026 to support potential ARIKAYCE label expansion to all patients with MAC lung disease. TPIP • Insmed has now enrolled more than 35% of patients in the Phase 3 PALM-ILD study of treprostinil palmitil inhalation powder (TPIP) in patients with pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and expects to complete enrollment in the first half of 2028. • In July 2026, Insmed enrolled its first patient in the Phase 3 PALM-PAH study of TPIP in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). • In September 2026, Insmed initiated the Phase 3 PALM-PPF study of TPIP in patients with progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF). • Insmed continues to anticipate initiating a Phase 3 study of TPIP in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) in the first half of 2027. INS1148 • Insmed continues to advance a Phase 2 development program for INS1148, initially targeting IPF, with plans to evaluate PPF and other diseases where inhibition of the pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic responses mediated by stem cell factor 248 (SCF248) may be beneficial. Immunology & Inflammation INS1033 • In September 2026, the Phase 1 study of INS1033, a dipeptidyl peptidase 1 (DPP1) inhibitor cleared by the FDA for patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), began active enrollment of healthy volunteers. Neuro & Other Rare INS1201 • Insmed completed enrollment of the Phase 1 ASCEND clinical study of INS1201, an intrathecally delivered gene therapy for patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). INS1202 • Insmed continues to enroll patients in the Phase 1 ARMOR study of INS1202, an intrathecally delivered gene therapy for patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). 2 Corporate Updates • In September 2026, Insmed presented five abstracts from across its Respiratory therapeutic area at the European Respiratory Society (ERS) Congress 2026. • In October 2026, Insmed presented data across its respiratory portfolio at the American College of Chest Physicians (CHEST) 2026 Annual Meeting and IDWeek 2026. • In October 2026, Insmed announced the appointment of Paul Hudson, former Chief Executive Officer of Sanofi and Novartis Pharmaceuticals, and Utpal Koppikar, current Chief Financial Officer of Verily Health, to its Board of Directors. Third-Quarter 2026 Financial Results The following table summarizes third-quarter and year-to-date 2026 and 2025 revenues and revenue growth for BRINSUPRI and ARIKAYCE across our commercial regions: INSMED INCORPORATED Revenue by Region (in millions) Three Months Ended September 30, Nine Months Ended September 30, (in millions) 2026 2025 Growth 2026 2025 Growth ARIKAYCE U.S. $ 75.5 $ 74.0 2% $ 208.6 $ 206.9 1% International 48.9 40.3 21% 130.2 107.6 21% Total $ 124.4 $ 114.3 9% $ 338.8 $ 314.5 8% BRINSUPRI U.S. $ 398.1 $ 28.1 NM $ 913.8 $ 28.1 NM International 2.0 - N/A 3.3 - N/A Total $ 400.1 $ 28.1 NM $ 917.1 $ 28.1 NM Total Revenues U.S. $ 473.6 $ 102.0 364% $ 1,122.4 $ 235.0 378% International 50.8 40.3 26% 133.5 107.6 24% Total $ 524.4 $ 142.3 268% $ 1,255.9 $ 342.6 267% • Cost of product revenues (excluding amortization of intangibles) were $78.2 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $29.4 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase in cost of product revenues in the third quarter of 2026 primarily reflects the increase in total product revenues for ARIKAYCE and BRINSUPRI. Cost of product revenues as a percentage of revenues decreased in the third quarter of 2026 due to sales of BRINSUPRI, which has lower manufacturing costs than ARIKAYCE. • Research and development (R&D) expenses were $270.0 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $186.4 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase in R&D expenses for the third quarter of 2026 was related to an increase in manufacturing costs, an increase in clinical development and research costs, both primarily related to TPIP, and an increase in compensation and benefit-related expenses and stock-based compensation costs due primarily to an increase in headcount. • Selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $253.0 million, compared to $186.4 million for the third quarter of 2025. title: STAT Plus: Merck, Isomorphic Labs partner to develop oncology drug candidates
content: STAT PlusExclusive Merck, Isomorphic Labs partner to develop oncology drug candidates Collaboration will focus on small molecules aimed at undisclosed oncology target Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Adobe By Katherine MacPhailNov. 19, 2026 Reporter, Live Journalism Katherine MacPhail[email protected]Katherine MacPhail is a reporter and editorial events programmer for STAT. Merck and Isomorphic Labs, the artificial intelligence drug designer built on a Nobel winning technology that can model how molecules will bind to proteins, said Thursday that they are entering into a research collaboration to discover small molecule candidates for an undisclosed oncology target of “strategic importance.” The partnership — only the latest such deal between a pharma giant and Isomorphic — will bring together the latter’s proprietary drug design engine and existing wet lab data from Merck, officials from both companies said. Merck will handle the preclinical and clinical development, manufacturing, and commercializing of any products. Advertisement “It is a target of high interest to us, a target where we have deployed internal efforts, and we think the pairing of those datasets with the Isomorphic drug discovery engine technology could be a very powerful pairing,” said George Addona, global head of discovery, preclinical development, and translational medicine at Merck.
